$comment: What each language promises and how the suite holds it; docs/languages/tiers.md says what this means. A profile is a set of scenarios by layer, or by a feature a scenario needs, and its description says what a language that holds it can do; a tier is what a language guarantees and when. The runner reads this on every run and refuses a scenario no profile places.

core.description: A peer of this language speaks the wire with a peer of any other: it sends and receives frames, correlates calls with their answers, cancels, closes with a code, applies backpressure, and refuses what the wire validator refuses, held against the reference on both sides of a socket.

generator.description: The generator renders this language: the packages it renders build against the language's runtime, hold the round trip and the generic-versus-bound diagram, and serve as well as call, including values carried over prepared channels and live callables, which is why holding it takes the tunnel and live runtimes too.

tunnel.description: A peer of this language multiplexes channels over one connection, with per-channel credit and closure, and reports the tunnel's events to its observer.

live.description: A peer of this language passes callable values across a connection: a scope over the peer exports bindings, imports references, releases and forwards them, and refuses a wrong contract or a stale reference.

observability.description: A peer of this language reports what it did, at every layer, under the common event names and never with a payload, and mints and carries trace context across calls.
